issues.description: validate_conda substring match treats 'anaconda' or paths containing 'mamba' as valid
issues.detail: The check `if any(tool in out.decode().lower() for tool in ["micromamba", "mamba", "conda"])` matches any substring in the --version output. 'anaconda 23.x' contains 'conda' which is fine, but 'mamba' is a substring of 'micromamba' (harmless here) and any future tool whose --version banner mentions one of these words would pass. Anchor with a regex like `^(conda|mamba|micromamba)\s+\d` to validate the leading tool name and a version token.

issues.description: filters='*.exe' restricts the file picker to Windows binaries on macOS/Linux
issues.detail: On POSIX systems, conda/mamba/micromamba executables have no extension. Passing `filters='*.exe'` to `create_browsefile` will hide every valid candidate in the native file dialog on Linux and macOS, forcing users to type the path. Make the filter platform-conditional (e.g. '*.exe' on Windows, '*' or no filter elsewhere) or drop it entirely and rely on `validate_conda`.

issues.description: run_program output not decoded safely and stderr is ignored, breaking validation for tools that print version to stderr
issues.detail: `run_program(...).communicate()` returns bytes; `out.decode()` uses the default encoding and will raise on non-UTF-8 locales. More importantly, some conda variants print `--version` to stderr — that output is discarded here, so valid executables can be rejected. Capture both streams, decode with errors='replace', and search the combined text.

issues.description: validate_conda has no timeout; a hung or interactive binary blocks the preferences dialog
issues.detail: If the user selects a non-conda executable that happens to be executable and waits on stdin (or hangs), `communicate()` blocks indefinitely with no timeout, freezing the settings UI thread. Pass `timeout=` to communicate and treat timeout as invalid, or wrap with a short deadline. Defense in depth against the user pointing at the wrong binary.

issues.description: Kernelspec reads conda_path even when find_conda() succeeds, ignoring user's explicit override
issues.detail: The new logic only consults `conda_path` when `find_conda()` returns nothing. A user who enables 'custom_conda' specifically to override a wrong auto-detected conda will be silently ignored. State the intended invariant explicitly: when `custom_conda` is set, the configured `conda_path` takes precedence over discovery. Otherwise the checkbox name misleads.

issues.description: create_browsefile API extension lacks a docstring or invariant for the new validate_callback/validate_reason contract
issues.detail: Two new parameters added to a widely-used helper with no documented contract: what should validate_callback return for empty input, is it called on every keystroke or only on commit, what happens if validate_reason is None while callback is set. A short docstring stating the invariant (returns bool, empty string is accepted, reason shown on False) prevents future misuse. The code is correct; the explanation is missing.

review.summary: The change is small and largely sensible: a new preference, a confpage entry, a validator, and a fallback in kernelspec. UNDER-AUDITED on the validator — substring matching against decoded stdout is loose, ignores stderr, has no timeout, and the file dialog filter assumes Windows. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on the kernelspec branching: the precedence between auto-detected conda and the user's explicit override should be stated as an invariant in the code, because the current order (auto wins) likely contradicts user intent. The widget API extension is correct but underdocumented for a shared helper. No algorithmic complexity concerns; the issues are correctness-by-analysis and readability, which is exactly what this lens looks for.
